steps.title: Character Concept
steps.description: What kind of hero do you want to play? Pick an archetype and jot a few notes—mechanical choices come next.

steps.title: Choose a Class
steps.description: Your class defines combat role, Max Wounds, and core features.

steps.title: Choose a Subclass
steps.description: At 2nd level in YMIAT you take a subclass—choose yours when building a level 2+ character.

steps.title: Determine Ability Scores
steps.description: Assign Fitness, Insight, and Willpower modifiers using your group's preferred method.

steps.title: Choose a Lineage
steps.description: Lineage traits shape ancestry and fundamental abilities.

steps.title: Choose a Heritage
steps.description: Heritage adds cultural flavor and extra traits. Any heritage works with any lineage—recommendations highlight common pairings.

steps.title: Choose a Background
steps.description: Background reflects life before adventuring—skills, gear, and a defining talent.

steps.title: Starting Equipment
steps.description: Take standard packages or roll starting wealth—confirm with your GM.

steps.title: Review Character
steps.description: Check your choices, copy a summary, or start over.

conceptArchetypes.label: Melee Combatant
conceptArchetypes.hint: Front-line fighter with sword, axe, or fist.

conceptArchetypes.label: Magic User
conceptArchetypes.hint: Spells to harm, heal, or control the field.

conceptArchetypes.label: Ranged Fighter
conceptArchetypes.hint: Bow, crossbow, or thrown weapons at distance.

conceptArchetypes.label: Support Character
conceptArchetypes.hint: Buff allies, heal, and control enemies.

conceptArchetypes.label: Hybrid Character
conceptArchetypes.hint: Blend martial prowess with magic or tactics.

abilityMethods.label: Standard Array
abilityMethods.description: Assign +2, +1, and +0 to Fitness, Insight, and Willpower in any order.

abilityMethods.label: Point-Buy
abilityMethods.description: Start at 0 with 3 points. Each ability may be −1 to +2; lowering one below 0 frees a point.

abilityMethods.label: Rolling (GM)
abilityMethods.description: Rolling is still being adapted for YMIAT—use another method or agree on rolls with your GM.

equipmentMethods.label: Class & background equipment
equipmentMethods.description: Take the gear listed for your class and background—fastest option at the table.

equipmentMethods.label: Starting wealth
equipmentMethods.description: Receive starting gold from your class and buy gear from the equipment lists.

classes.name: Barbarian
classes.summary: A primal warrior who channels fury in battle. High Max Wounds, melee dominance, and resistance while raging.
classes.proficiencies: Light and medium armor, shields, simple and martial weapons, herbalism tools. Skills: choose two from Animal Handling, Athletics, Intimidation, Nature, Perception, Survival.

abilities.name: Danger Sense
abilities.summary: Advantage on Fitness saves against unseen peril.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Advantage on Fitness saves against unseen peril.

You gain an uncanny sense of when things are not as they should be. You have advantage on Fitness saving throws unless you have the Incapacitated condition.

abilities.name: Rage
abilities.summary: Primal fury as a free action; bonus damage and physical resilience.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Primal fury as a free action; bonus damage and physical resilience.

In battle, you fight with primal ferocity. On your turn, you can rage as a free action.

While raging (and not wearing heavy armor):

  • You have advantage on Fitness ability checks and saves.
  • When you make a melee weapon attack using Fitness, you gain a bonus to damage per the Rage + column on your progression table.
  • You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage—attackers have disadvantage on those damage rolls against you.

You cannot cast spells or concentrate on them while raging.

Your rage lasts 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked unconscious, or if your turn ends and you have not attacked a hostile creature or taken damage from one since the start of your last turn. You can end rage early as a free action.

Uses per long rest: see the Rages column on your progression table.

abilities.name: Reckless Attack
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Trade defense for ferocious accuracy.

When you make an attack on your turn, you can attack recklessly. You have advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Fitness during this turn, but you have disadvantage on your Defense roll until the start of your next turn.

abilities.name: Unarmored Defense
abilities.summary: High AC without armor when relying on raw toughness.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
High AC without armor when relying on raw toughness.

While you are not wearing armor, your base Armor Class equals 10 + 2 × your Fitness modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

abilities.name: Fast Movement
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Extra speed and opening repositioning.

Your speed increases by 10 feet while you are not wearing heavy armor. When combat begins and you are not surprised, you can move up to half your speed before any turns are taken. This movement does not use your movement on your turn.

abilities.name: Feral Instinct
abilities.summary: First-turn ferocity and surprise immunity when raging.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
First-turn ferocity and surprise immunity when raging.

On the first turn of each combat, you have advantage on melee weapon attack rolls (circumstantial advantage; you still add PB if proficient with the weapon).

If you are surprised at the start of combat and are not incapacitated, you can act normally on your first turn if you enter a rage before doing anything else on that turn.

When using the initiative variant, you have advantage on initiative rolls.

abilities.name: Improvement
abilities.summary: Ability increases or a martial talent.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Ability increases or a martial talent.

At 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th, and 10th level, choose one improvement (ability modifiers cannot exceed +7 with this feature):

  • Increase a single ability modifier by 2.
  • Increase two different ability modifiers by 1 each.
  • Increase one ability modifier by 1 and select a talent from the martial talents list.

abilities.name: Multiattack
abilities.summary: Two attacks with the Attack action.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Two attacks with the Attack action.

Your physical prowess has grown. On your turn, you can make up to two attacks when you take the Attack action.

In YMIAT, each successful weapon attack typically inflicts 1 Wound (2 on a critical hit). Weapon bonuses apply to hit, not to the number of Wounds dealt.

abilities.name: Brutal Critical
abilities.summary: Expanded critical range and extra critical damage dice.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Expanded critical range and extra critical damage dice.

You score a critical hit on a d20 roll of 19 or 20 with melee weapons and unarmed strikes.

You also roll additional weapon damage dice on melee critical hits:

  • 5th level: 1 extra die
  • 7th level: 2 extra dice
  • 9th level: 3 extra dice

On a critical hit in YMIAT, the attack inflicts 2 Wounds before applying extra dice (exploding 20s still apply).

abilities.name: Heroic Boon
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Choose a powerful rage-enhancing boon.

Choose one heroic boon:

  • Instant Rage. When combat begins and you use Fast Movement's opening move, you can enter a rage without spending a free action if you have a use of Rage remaining.
  • Stubborn Rage. Your rage ends only when its duration expires, you fall unconscious, or you choose to end it.
  • Bloody Rage. While raging, slashing damage from your weapon attacks ignores resistance.
  • Vengeful Rage. When a hostile creature damages you while you are raging, you have stacking advantage on the first attack you make against that creature on your next turn.

abilities.name: Relentless Rage
abilities.summary: Cling to consciousness while raging at Max Wounds.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Cling to consciousness while raging at Max Wounds.

While raging, if your Wounds reach your Max Wounds, you can make a DC 10 Fitness save. On a success, you do not fall unconscious until your rage ends. You still make Life Saves as normal.

Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. The DC resets when you finish a short or long rest.

abilities.name: Unyielding Might
abilities.summary: Reliable Fitness and devastating blows against objects.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Reliable Fitness and devastating blows against objects.

When you make an ability check or save using Fitness, treat any d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

Your melee weapon attacks deal additional damage equal to your Fitness score (not modifier) against objects and structures.

abilities.name: Epic Boon
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Embody untamed power.

Primal Champion. Your Fitness modifier increases by 2. Your maximum Fitness modifier is now +7.

subclasses.name: Berserker
subclasses.summary: Primal bloodlust pushes your rage into a devastating frenzy.

features.name: Frenzy
features.summary: Optional frenzy with rage; extra melee attack while frenzied.
features.descriptionHtml:
Optional frenzy with rage; extra melee attack while frenzied.

When you rage, you can choose to enter a frenzy as part of the same free action.

While frenzied, once per turn you can make one extra melee weapon attack as your second action (you must not have moved this turn, per YMIAT second-action rules).

features.name: Ruthless Bearing
features.summary: Intimidation proficiency; Expertise (+2×PB) if already proficient.
features.descriptionHtml:
Intimidation proficiency; Expertise if already proficient.

You gain proficiency in the Intimidation skill. If you are already proficient, you gain Expertise instead: add +2×PB on Intimidation checks.

features.name: Mindless Rage
features.summary: Ignore exhaustion while raging; immune to charm and frighten; temp HP on crit or kill during frenzy.
features.descriptionHtml:
Ignore exhaustion while raging; immune to charm and frighten; temp HP on crit or kill during frenzy.

While raging, you gain the following benefits:

  • You ignore any levels of exhaustion for the duration of your rage.
  • You can't be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are already charmed or frightened when you enter a rage, the effect is suspended for the duration.
  • During a frenzy, if you score a critical hit or reduce a creature to 0 Wounds, you gain temporary Wounds equal to your PB + your Fitness modifier. These last until expended or until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Intimidating Presence
features.summary: Bonus damage vs. frightened foes; free action to frighten nearby creatures.
features.descriptionHtml:
Bonus damage vs. frightened foes; free action to frighten nearby creatures.

Your weapon attacks deal extra damage equal to your PB (same damage type as the weapon) to frightened creatures.

As a free action, you can attempt to frighten up to PB creatures within 30 feet that can see or hear you. Each target makes an Insight save (DC 8 + PB + Willpower modifier + temporary Wounds from Mindless Rage). On a failure, a creature is frightened of you until the end of your next turn.

On subsequent turns, you can use a free action to extend the effect on each frightened creature until the end of your next turn. The effect ends if the creature ends its turn more than 60 feet away or can no longer see or hear you. On a successful save, you can't use this feature on that creature again for 24 hours.

features.name: Retaliation
features.summary: Reaction: close on attacker and strike back.
features.descriptionHtml:
Reaction: close on attacker and strike back.

When a creature hits or misses you with an attack, you can use your reaction to move up to half your speed toward that creature and make a single melee attack against it. If the creature is Large or larger, you have advantage on the attack roll.

subclasses.name: Wild Fury
subclasses.summary: Animal spirits guide your rage—choose a beast focus at each subclass level.

features.name: Animal Focus
features.summary: Choose your first animal focus (2nd level in YMIAT).
features.descriptionHtml:
Choose your first animal focus (2nd level in YMIAT).

At 2nd level, choose an animal focus that shapes how your rage manifests. You choose another focus at 4th, 6th, and 8th level.

Options include: Alligator, Bear, Tiger, Toad, Hawk, Lizard, Turtle, Wolf, Crane, Ram, Shark, and Snake. Each focus grants a thematic benefit while you rage (movement, senses, damage type, or defense). Work with your GM to apply the BFRD Wild Fury focus rules adapted to YMIAT.

features.name: Deepening Focus
features.summary: Second animal focus (4th level in YMIAT).
features.descriptionHtml:
Second animal focus (4th level in YMIAT).

Choose a second animal focus. Its benefits stack with your first while you rage.

features.name: Primal Synthesis
features.summary: Third animal focus (6th level in YMIAT).
features.descriptionHtml:
Third animal focus (6th level in YMIAT).

Choose a third animal focus. When you rage, you can blend two active focuses for one enhanced effect once per rage.

features.name: Apex Predator
features.summary: Fourth animal focus (8th level in YMIAT).
features.descriptionHtml:
Fourth animal focus (8th level in YMIAT).

Choose a fourth animal focus. While raging, you can move up to half your speed when you enter a rage. Once per combat, if you enter a rage on your first turn, the first successful melee attack you make that turn deals 2 Wounds instead of 1 (unless it is already a critical hit).

subclasses.name: Chaos
subclasses.summary: Entropic fury warps the battlefield around your rage.

features.name: Chaos Manifestation
features.summary: Random surge on crit or dropping foes with spell attacks.

features.name: Chaos Origin Spells
features.summary: Always-known chaos origin spells.

features.name: Volatile Magic
features.summary: Leveled spells may trigger extra volatile effects.

features.name: Embrace Chaos
features.summary: Bonus action: suffer a volatile effect for sorcery points or temp Wounds.

features.name: Inflict Disorder
features.summary: Redirect volatile effects onto attackers.

features.name: Apotheosis of Discord
features.summary: 6th-level+ spells trigger a minute of chaotic mastery.

subclasses.name: Four Winds
subclasses.summary: Elemental winds empower your movement and strikes.

features.name: Implacable Presence
features.summary: Acrobatics proficiency or double PB on Acrobatics checks.
features.descriptionHtml:
Acrobatics proficiency or double PB on Acrobatics checks.

You gain proficiency in Acrobatics. If you are already proficient, add double your PB to Acrobatics checks instead.

features.name: Winds of Wrath
features.summary: Rage grants wind protection, thunder leaps, or thrown-weapon recklessness.
features.descriptionHtml:
Rage grants wind protection, thunder leaps, or thrown-weapon recklessness.

When you enter a rage, swirling winds surround you. While raging and conscious, you can't be knocked prone and always land on your feet after falling.

When you first enter a rage, choose one benefit for its duration:

  • Buffeting winds: lightly obscured; ranged attacks against you at disadvantage; resistance to lightning and thunder.
  • Thunder leap: if you leap 10+ feet toward a foe and hit with melee on the same turn, add 1d6 thunder per 10 feet traveled (max 10d6). On any thunder damage, Fitness save (DC = damage dealt) or prone.
  • Thrown wrath: Reckless Attack with thrown weapons using Fitness; thrown range doubled; double rage damage bonus on the throw.

When you enter a rage, you can expend an additional Rage use to take a second option.

features.name: Cyclonic Ward
features.summary: Reduce falling damage; reaction to shield allies and reposition them.
features.descriptionHtml:
Reduce falling damage; reaction to shield allies and reposition them.

Reduce falling damage by twice your barbarian level (after rage halving while raging).

While raging, as a reaction when you or an ally within 30 feet takes damage, reduce that damage by your barbarian level and move the ally up to 10 feet (if willing).

features.name: Howling Charge
features.summary: Free action Dash; ignore difficult terrain and paralysis/restraint until next turn.
features.descriptionHtml:
Free action Dash; ignore difficult terrain and paralysis/restraint until next turn.

As a free action, take the Dash action. Until the start of your next turn, ignore difficult terrain and you can't be paralyzed or restrained.

features.name: Raging Storm
features.summary: Thunder aura on hits; cyclonic retaliation and lightning throws.
features.descriptionHtml:
Thunder aura on hits; cyclonic retaliation and lightning throws.

While raging:

  • Each melee or unarmed hit deals 1d6 thunder to the target and each hostile creature within 10 feet.
  • When you use Cyclonic Ward against a melee attack, the attacker makes a Fitness save (DC 8 + PB + Fitness) or takes 4d6 thunder (half on success). Fail by 5+ = deafened 1 minute.
  • First thrown weapon hit (Fitness) each turn: target and creatures within 10 feet take 3d6 lightning.

Thunder from Raging Storm is audible out to 300 feet.

subclasses.name: Kraken
subclasses.summary: Crushing tentacle-like force and abyssal resilience.

features.name: Deep Vision
features.summary: Swim speed, water breathing, enhanced darkvision underwater.
features.descriptionHtml:
Swim speed, water breathing, enhanced darkvision underwater.

You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed and can breathe water. While submerged, you gain darkvision 60 feet (or +30 feet if you already have darkvision).

features.name: Kraken's Grasp
features.summary: Spectral tentacles while raging: grapple, damage scaling d4→d10.
features.descriptionHtml:
Spectral tentacles while raging: grapple, damage scaling d4→d10.

When you rage, two spectral tentacles sprout (reach 10 ft., proficient melee weapons). As a free action when you rage (or later on your turn), make up to two tentacle attacks (one per tentacle). On hit: force damage = tentacle die + Fitness modifier; Large or smaller targets are grappled (escape DC 8 + PB + Fitness). A grappling tentacle can attack only its grappled target.

Tentacle damage die scales: d4 (2nd), d6 (4th), d8 (6th), d10 (8th). Tentacles can lift objects up to Fitness × PB pounds and perform simple tasks (not wield weapons or use tools).

features.name: Ink Cloud
features.summary: Free action inky obscurement you can see through.
features.descriptionHtml:
Free action inky obscurement you can see through.

As a free action, create a stationary 20-foot-radius heavily obscured sphere centered on you. You see normally inside it. Lasts 1 minute or until dismissed. PB uses per long rest.

features.name: Titan Grip
features.summary: Grappled foes restrained; tentacles can replace Attack action attacks.
features.descriptionHtml:
Grappled foes restrained; tentacles can replace Attack action attacks.

Creatures grappled by your tentacles are restrained until the grapple ends. When you take the Attack action, you can use tentacles for any number of your attacks.

features.name: Tentacle Fling
features.summary: Hurl grappled foes up to 30 feet for falling damage.
features.descriptionHtml:
Hurl grappled foes up to 30 feet for falling damage.

When you take the Attack action, you can use one or more attacks to throw a tentacle-grappled creature up to 30 feet. It lands prone; bludgeoning damage 1d6 per 10 feet thrown (also to a struck creature on failed Fitness save, DC 8 + PB + Fitness).

features.name: Leviathan Wakes
features.summary: +10 ft tentacle reach; one extra tentacle attack per free action.
features.descriptionHtml:
+10 ft tentacle reach; one extra tentacle attack per free action.

Tentacle reach increases by 10 feet. Each time you use a free action for tentacle attacks, you can make one additional tentacle attack as part of that same free action.

classes.name: Bard
classes.summary: A versatile performer whose magic and inspiration support allies and confound foes.
classes.proficiencies: Light armor; simple weapons and martial finesse weapons; three musical instruments or tools; any three skills.
classes.spellcasting: Arcane spells. Spells known (no preparation). Rituals known per level.

abilities.name: Bardic Inspiration
abilities.summary: Grant an inspiration die to bolster an ally's roll.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Grant an inspiration die to bolster an ally's roll.

As an action, choose one creature other than yourself within 60 feet that can hear or see you. That creature gains one Bardic Inspiration die (d6 at 1st level, d8 at 4th, d10 at 7th).

Within the next 10 minutes, the creature can roll the die and add the result to one ability check, attack roll, or save. The die is then lost.

Uses per long rest equal to your Willpower modifier (minimum 1). See Font of Inspiration at 3rd level.

abilities.name: Expertise
abilities.descriptionHtml:
+2×PB on chosen skills or tools.

Choose two skill or tool proficiencies (or one of each). You have Expertise with them: add +2×PB instead of +PB on ability checks that use either proficiency.

At 5th level, choose two more proficiencies to gain this benefit.

abilities.name: Spellcasting
abilities.summary: Arcane spells known; uses Spell Power.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Arcane spells known; uses Spell Power.

As a conduit for Arcane magic, you cast spells using Spell Power (SP). Spell cost equals spell level. Your max spell level by character level is shown on the Bard progression table.

You know a fixed list of spells and do not prepare them daily. Learn additional spells at the levels shown on your class progression table.

Spellcasting ability: Willpower (WIL). Spell save DC and spell attack modifier use your proficiency bonus + Willpower (WIL) modifier.

Cantrips & rituals: As shown on your progression table. Rituals do not cost Spell Power when cast using the ritual rules in Magic.

Second action casting: If you cast a spell as your second action (because you did not move this turn), spell attacks are at disadvantage and targets have advantage on saves against that spell.

abilities.name: Bardic Performance
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Weave magic into ongoing performances.

As an action, begin a performance (Celebrate Life, Cutting Words, or Clarity of Thought at 5th level). Maintain it by spending an action at the start of each of your turns, up to 1 minute.

  • Celebrate Life. Allies in range can expend a Recovery die at the start of their turn to heal; allies have advantage on Life Saves.
  • Cutting Words. Reaction while performing: subtract an inspiration die from an enemy's check, attack, or damage roll.
  • Clarity of Thought (5th). Allies in range cannot be charmed and have advantage on saves against fear.

Uses per long rest equal to your proficiency bonus.

abilities.name: Font of Inspiration
abilities.summary: Regain inspiration on short rest; bolster failed rolls.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Regain inspiration on short rest; bolster failed rolls.

You regain all expended uses of Bardic Inspiration when you finish a short or long rest.

When a creature within 60 feet fails a check, attack, or save, you can use your reaction to expend inspiration and add the die to the total, potentially turning failure into success.

abilities.name: Improvement
abilities.summary: Ability increases or a utility talent.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Ability increases or a utility talent.

At 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th, and 10th level, choose one improvement (ability modifiers cannot exceed +7 with this feature):

  • Increase a single ability modifier by 2.
  • Increase two different ability modifiers by 1 each.
  • Increase one ability modifier by 1 and select a talent from the utility talents list.

abilities.name: Heroic Boon
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Persistent or valiant inspiration options.

Choose one:

  • Persistent Inspiration. If a creature adds your inspiration die and still fails, the die is not lost.
  • Valiant Inspiration. After a successful attack, the creature can expend the die for extra damage; or as a reaction when taking damage, reduce damage by die + your Willpower modifier.

abilities.name: Magical Secrets
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Learn spells from any source.

Choose two spells (or cantrips) from any spell list at 6th level and two more at 9th. Each must be of a level you can cast. They count as Arcane spells for you.

abilities.name: Grand Performance
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Performance range increases to 60 feet.

Your Bardic Performance now affects creatures within 60 feet that can hear or see you.

abilities.name: Epic Boon
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Recover inspiration during performance.

Curtain Call. If you start your turn with no Bardic Inspiration uses remaining, you can recover uses equal to your Willpower modifier (minimum 1) as part of the action that maintains your performance. Once per long rest.

subclasses.name: Lore
subclasses.summary: A collector of knowledge who weaves magic and talents from every tradition.

features.name: Bardic Performance: Ode to Heroes
features.summary: Performance that helps allies and hinders foes on ability checks.
features.descriptionHtml:
Performance that helps allies and hinders foes on ability checks.

You gain the Ode to Heroes Bardic Performance option. When you perform, choose Fitness, Insight, or Willpower. While your performance lasts, allies in range have advantage on ability checks using that ability and enemies have disadvantage.

features.name: Expanded Talent List
features.summary: Choose talents from magic or utility lists.
features.descriptionHtml:
Choose talents from magic or utility lists.

When you gain a new talent from Improvement, you can select it from either the magic or utility talent lists.

features.name: Jack of All Trades
features.summary: Half PB on ability checks that don't already include PB.
features.descriptionHtml:
Half PB on ability checks that don't already include PB.

Add half your PB (rounded down) to any ability check that doesn't already include your PB.

features.name: Swift Ritual
features.summary: Cast a known ritual as an action once per long rest.
features.descriptionHtml:
Cast a known ritual as an action once per long rest.

You can cast an Arcane ritual you know as an action instead of its listed casting time. You must still provide all other components. Once used, you can't use this again until you finish a long rest.

features.name: Magical Rites
features.summary: Learn two extra ritual spells from any source.
features.descriptionHtml:
Learn two extra ritual spells from any source.

Learn two ritual spells of your choice from any source list. Each must be of a level you can cast. They count as Arcane spells for you and don't count against rituals known from your class table.

features.name: Peerless Skill
features.summary: Spend Bardic Inspiration on ability checks; keep the die on success.
features.descriptionHtml:
Spend Bardic Inspiration on ability checks; keep the die on success.

When you make an ability check and have Bardic Inspiration available, you can roll a Bardic Inspiration die and add it to the check. If you succeed, you keep the die; if you fail, the die is expended.

subclasses.name: Victory
subclasses.summary: Inspire allies to triumph through martial cadence.

features.name: Bardic Performance: Battle March
features.summary: Performance lets allies react-move; medium armor and martial weapon.
features.descriptionHtml:
Performance lets allies react-move; medium armor and martial weapon.

You gain Battle March as a Bardic Performance option. When you perform—and as part of each free action spent maintaining it—you can command up to three willing allies who can see or hear you to use their reaction to move up to half their speed without opportunity attacks.

You also gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and one martial weapon of your choice.

When Improvement grants a new talent, you can choose from the martial or utility talent lists.

features.name: Multiattack
features.summary: Two attacks when you take the Attack action.
features.descriptionHtml:
Two attacks when you take the Attack action.

When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make two attacks instead of one.

features.name: Unified Front
features.summary: Reaction: boost your save and allies auto-succeed on area effects.
features.descriptionHtml:
Reaction: boost your save and allies auto-succeed on area effects.

When you are targeted by an area effect that requires a save, use your reaction to expend a Bardic Inspiration die and add it to your save. On a success, every friendly creature in the area automatically succeeds on their saves as well.

features.name: Inspired Strike
features.summary: Spend Bardic Inspiration on attacks; keep the die on a hit.
features.descriptionHtml:
Spend Bardic Inspiration on attacks; keep the die on a hit.

Once per turn when you make a weapon or spell attack and have Bardic Inspiration available, roll a Bardic Inspiration die and add it to the attack roll. If you hit, you keep the die; if you miss, the die is expended.

subclasses.summary: Bards who align with the college of Allure understand the power of the mind and how the smallest nudge can bend that power in their favor. These bards are masters of subtle

features.summary: You weave illusions to protect your companions. When
features.descriptionHtml:

subclasses.summary: Bards aligned with the college of Mockery have devoted their lives to perfecting their mordant repartee—both to entertain audiences and to use as a devastating weapon

features.name: Bardic Performance: Playful Banter
features.summary: Your jests and banter bolster your allies’ defenses against
features.descriptionHtml:
Your jests and banter bolster your allies’ defenses against

Your jests and banter bolster your allies’ defenses against similar assaults on the mind. While your performance lasts, each ally within range that takes psychic damage reduces that damage by an amount equal to your bard level + your

features.name: Razor Wit
features.summary: You learn the vicious mockery cantrip and the hideous laughter
features.descriptionHtml:
You learn the vicious mockery cantrip and the hideous laughter

You learn the vicious mockery cantrip and the hideous laughter spell if you don’t already know them. When you cast vicious mockery, you add your CHA modifier to the damage roll.

features.name: Infectious Laughter
features.summary: When you cast vicious mockery, you can target a number
features.descriptionHtml:
When you cast vicious mockery, you can target a number

When you cast vicious mockery, you can target a number of creatures equal to one + half your PB (rounded down).

features.name: Crushing Jest
features.summary: Your insults are so crushing that even creatures with
features.descriptionHtml:
Your insults are so crushing that even creatures with

Your insults are so crushing that even creatures with strong mental defenses wilt beneath the verbal assault.

features.name: Mocking Rage
features.summary: Your banter and mockery can enrage creatures. As an
features.descriptionHtml:
Your banter and mockery can enrage creatures. As an

Your banter and mockery can enrage creatures. As an action, choose a number of creatures up to your PB that you can see within 30 feet of you. Each target must make a WIS save against your spell save DC or succumb to a fit of rage for 1 minute. While in such a fit, a target is unable to distinguish friend from foe and must attack the nearest creature on its turn. If no other creature is near enough to move to and attack, the target stalks off in a random direction, seeking a target for its rage. A target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

features.descriptionHtml:
You learn the message and thaumaturgy cantrips and the

You learn the message and thaumaturgy cantrips and the silence spell if you don’t already know them. These spells count as Arcane spells when you cast them, but they don’t count against the number of cantrips or spells you know as listed in the Bard Progression table (see Player’s Guide).

features.name: Bardic Performance: Spell
features.summary: The bard class receives new features and subclasses in this
features.descriptionHtml:
The bard class receives new features and subclasses in this

The bard class receives new features and subclasses in this section.

classes.name: Cleric
classes.summary: A divine champion who channels deity power through spells and channel divinity.
classes.proficiencies: Light and medium armor, shields, simple weapons. Skills: History, Insight, Medicine, Persuasion, Religion (choose two).
classes.spellcasting: Divine spells (prepared). Domain spells always prepared.

abilities.name: Manifestation of Faith
abilities.summary: Holy warrior or miracle worker path.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Holy warrior or miracle worker path.

Choose how you manifest your faith:

  • Manifest Might. Proficiency with heavy armor and one martial weapon. Once per turn when you hit with a weapon attack, deal extra radiant or necrotic damage equal to your proficiency bonus.
  • Manifest Miracles. Learn one extra cantrip from any source (counts as Divine). Add your proficiency bonus to damage dealt by your Divine cantrips.

abilities.name: Spellcasting
abilities.summary: Prepared Divine spells using Spell Power.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Prepared Divine spells using Spell Power.

As a conduit for Divine magic, you cast spells using Spell Power (SP). Spell cost equals spell level. Your max spell level by character level is shown on the Cleric progression table.

You prepare spells in advance. You can prepare a number of spells equal to your Insight (INS) modifier + your cleric level (minimum one). Change your prepared list during a long rest.

Spellcasting ability: Insight (INS). Spell save DC and spell attack modifier use your proficiency bonus + Insight (INS) modifier.

Cantrips & rituals: As shown on your progression table. Rituals do not cost Spell Power when cast using the ritual rules in Magic.

Second action casting: If you cast a spell as your second action (because you did not move this turn), spell attacks are at disadvantage and targets have advantage on saves against that spell.

abilities.name: Channel Divinity
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Channel divine energy beyond spells.

You channel divine energy as a free action. You start with Turn the Profane. Uses: 1/rest at 2nd, 2/rest at 5th, 3/rest at 9th. Regain all uses on a short or long rest.

See Turn the Profane and Destroy the Profane.

abilities.name: Turn the Profane
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Turn fiends and undead.

As an action, present your holy symbol. Each Fiend and Undead of your choice within 30 feet that can see or hear you makes an Insight save against your spell save DC. On a failure, the creature is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage.

A turned creature must move away from you and can only Dash or Dodge on its turn.

abilities.name: Improvement
abilities.summary: Ability increases or a magic talent.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Ability increases or a magic talent.

At 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th, and 10th level, choose one improvement (ability modifiers cannot exceed +7 with this feature):

  • Increase a single ability modifier by 2.
  • Increase two different ability modifiers by 1 each.
  • Increase one ability modifier by 1 and select a talent from the magic talents list.

abilities.name: Destroy the Profane
abilities.summary: Destroy turned creatures below a CR threshold.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Destroy turned creatures below a CR threshold.

When a Fiend or Undead fails its save against Turn the Profane, it is instantly destroyed if its CR is at or below:

  • 4th level: CR ½
  • 6th level: CR 1
  • 8th level: CR 2
  • 10th level: CR 4

abilities.name: Heroic Boon
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Consecration or wrath gifts.

Choose one:

  • Gift of Consecration. Immune to disease, poison damage, and poisoned. If you die, your body is preserved as gentle repose for up to a year.
  • Gift of Wrath. Resistance to radiant or necrotic (your choice). When you cast a damaging spell, you can change its damage type to radiant or necrotic.

abilities.name: Divine Intervention
abilities.summary: Call on your deity in dire need.
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Call on your deity in dire need.

At the start of your turn, roll d20 + proficiency bonus. On a 19 or lower, your deity does not intervene. On 20+, your deity intervenes.

On intervention, use your action to cast any Divine spell (or domain spell) of casting time action without spending Spell Power. If the level exceeds your max, make a spellcasting ability check DC 10 + level.

After a successful intervention, you cannot use this feature again for 1 week (or until a long rest once you have Epic Boon: Divine Herald).

abilities.name: Epic Boon
abilities.descriptionHtml:
Automatic divine intervention.

Divine Herald. Divine Intervention succeeds automatically. You no longer wait a week between uses, though you can still use it only once per long rest.

subclasses.name: Life
subclasses.summary: Celebrate vitality and oppose the perversion of undeath.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
features.summary: Channel divinity to distribute healing among nearby allies.
features.descriptionHtml:
Channel divinity to distribute healing among nearby allies.

As an action, present your holy symbol and restore Wounds equal to 5 × your cleric level, divided among creatures within 30 feet. No creature can be restored above half its Max Wounds. No effect on Constructs or Undead.

features.name: Disciple of Life
features.summary: Healing spells restore extra Wounds.
features.descriptionHtml:
Healing spells restore extra Wounds.

When you cast a Divine spell of 1st level or higher to restore Wounds, the target regains 2 + the spell's level additional Wounds.

features.name: Life Domain Spells
features.summary: Always-prepared life domain spells.
features.descriptionHtml:
Always-prepared life domain spells.

These domain spells are always prepared:

  • Level 2: bless, cure wounds, gentle repose, restoration
  • Level 5: mass healing word, revivify
  • Level 7: death ward, guardian of faith
  • Level 9: greater restoration, mass cure wounds

features.name: Blessed Healer
features.summary: Healing others heals you.
features.descriptionHtml:
Healing others heals you.

When you cast a Divine spell of 1st level or higher that restores Wounds to another creature, you regain 2 + the spell's level Wounds.

features.name: Greater Preservation
features.summary: Expanded Preserve Life with condition cleansing.
features.descriptionHtml:
Expanded Preserve Life with condition cleansing.

Preserve Life affects creatures within 60 feet. When you use it, one target can also: cure all diseases; end blinded, deafened, paralyzed, or poisoned; or neutralize all poisons.

features.name: Perfect Healing
features.summary: Healing spells restore maximum Wounds.
features.descriptionHtml:
Healing spells restore maximum Wounds.

When you cast a Divine spell of 1st level or higher that restores Wounds, you automatically restore the maximum possible Wounds (no dice rolling).

subclasses.name: Light
subclasses.summary: Wield radiant fire and searing truth against darkness.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Searing Radiance
features.summary: Channel radiance through your magical lights.
features.descriptionHtml:
Channel radiance through your magical lights.

As an action, present your holy symbol and channel radiance through every magical light source you created on the same plane. Each hostile creature in their bright light makes a Fitness save. Roll 2 × PB d8s; failed save = full radiant damage, success = half. Aberrations and Undead have disadvantage.

features.name: Imbue Light
features.summary: Learn light and dancing lights; dancing lights needs no concentration.
features.descriptionHtml:
Learn light and dancing lights; dancing lights needs no concentration.

You learn light and dancing lights if you don't know them. Dancing lights requires no concentration and lasts for the duration or until you cast it again. Both count as Divine cantrips and don't count against cantrips known.

features.name: Light Domain Spells
features.summary: Always-prepared light domain spells.
features.descriptionHtml:
Always-prepared light domain spells.

These domain spells are always prepared:

  • Level 2: burning hands, guiding bolt, moonbeam, scorching ray
  • Level 5: daylight, fireball
  • Level 7: elemental shield, wall of fire
  • Level 9: dispel evil and good, flame strike

features.name: Overwhelming Flash
features.summary: Reaction penalizes nearby attack rolls with blinding light.
features.descriptionHtml:
Reaction penalizes nearby attack rolls with blinding light.

When a creature within 10 feet makes an attack roll, use your reaction to release divine light. The attacker takes a penalty equal to your Insight modifier on the roll. If the attack still hits, the attacker is blinded until end of its turn. PB uses per long rest.

features.name: Radiant Spellcasting
features.summary: Cantrips and lit weapons deal extra radiant damage.
features.descriptionHtml:
Cantrips and lit weapons deal extra radiant damage.

Your Divine damaging cantrips deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage. While holding a weapon under light or continual flame, the first time it deals damage each turn, add radiant damage equal to your Insight modifier.

features.name: Lux Malediction
features.summary: Searing Radiance becomes sunlight; Overwhelming Flash curses foes.
features.descriptionHtml:
Searing Radiance becomes sunlight; Overwhelming Flash curses foes.

Searing Radiance makes your lights magical sunlight for 1 minute. When you use Overwhelming Flash, curse the target (one at a time): can't regain Wounds until end of next turn; radiant damage = cleric level; −10 Insight (Perception) for 10 minutes; or can't benefit from invisibility for 1 minute. Remove curse ends it; magical darkness on both turns ends it.

features.name: Luminous Shroud
features.summary: Advantage on saves in bright light; charm/frighten immunity; damage choice.
features.descriptionHtml:
Advantage on saves in bright light; charm/frighten immunity; damage choice.

While in bright light, you have advantage on saves, can't be charmed or frightened, and gain immunity to radiant damage or resistance to necrotic damage (your choice).

subclasses.name: War
subclasses.summary: Champion courage and decisive victory in battle.

features.name: Channel Divinity: Mark of Triumph
features.summary: Mark a foe so allies gain advantage on the first attack against it.
features.descriptionHtml:
Mark a foe so allies gain advantage on the first attack against it.

As a free action, present your holy symbol and mark one creature within 60 feet you can see. Until the start of your next turn, the first attack roll each ally makes against the marked creature has advantage.

features.name: Disciple of War
features.summary: Extra weapon attack when you hit with the Attack action.
features.descriptionHtml:
Extra weapon attack when you hit with the Attack action.

Once per turn when you hit with a weapon attack during the Attack action, you can make one additional weapon attack as part of that same action. Uses per short or long rest equal to your PB.

features.name: Expanded Talent List
features.summary: Martial or magic talents on Improvement.
features.descriptionHtml:
Martial or magic talents on Improvement.

When you gain a talent from Improvement, you can choose from the magic or martial talent lists.

features.name: War Domain Spells
features.summary: Always-prepared war domain spells.
features.descriptionHtml:
Always-prepared war domain spells.

These domain spells are always prepared:

  • Level 2: command, magic weapon, shield of faith, warding bond
  • Level 5: fear, spirit guardians
  • Level 7: death ward, guardian of faith
  • Level 9: antilife shell, flame strike

features.name: Blessed Warrior
features.summary: Martial weapon proficiency and Fitness-based attacks.
features.descriptionHtml:
Martial weapon proficiency and Fitness-based attacks.

You gain proficiency with martial weapons. You can use Fitness for attack and damage rolls with martial weapons.

features.name: Greater Triumph
features.summary: Marked creatures have disadvantage on saves against your spells.
features.descriptionHtml:
Marked creatures have disadvantage on saves against your spells.

Creatures marked by Mark of Triumph have disadvantage on saves against your Divine spells until the mark ends.

features.name: Holy Strike
features.summary: Weapon attacks deal extra radiant damage once per turn.
features.descriptionHtml:
Weapon attacks deal extra radiant damage once per turn.

Once per turn when you hit with a weapon attack, the attack deals 1d8 radiant damage in addition to the weapon's damage.

subclasses.name: Death
subclasses.summary: Gods of the Death domain govern death and the afterlife, exemplifying the inevitability and mystery of the beyond. Devotees of this domain bring peace to the bereaved,

features.name: Channel Divinity: Forsee Doom
features.summary: Death Domain Spells, Death’s Sentinel
features.descriptionHtml:
Death Domain Spells, Death’s Sentinel

Death Domain Spells, Death’s Sentinel 7th

subclasses.name: Nature
subclasses.summary: Gods of the Nature domain protect and govern the overgrown wilds and fertile lands. Dogmatic followers of this domain are entrusted with the safety and prosperity

features.name: Apostle of Nature
features.summary: You gain proficiency in any two of the following skills or
features.descriptionHtml:
You gain proficiency in any two of the following skills or

You gain proficiency in any two of the following skills or tools: Animal Handling, Nature, Survival; herbalist tools, land vehicles, or water vehicles.

subclasses.name: Tempest
subclasses.summary: Gods of the Tempest domain embody the awesome destructive power of storms, earthquakes, wildfires, and similar natural disasters. Clerics of this domain are often as

features.name: Channel Divinity: Storm’s Fury
features.summary: You can use your Channel Divinity feature to invoke the
features.descriptionHtml:
You can use your Channel Divinity feature to invoke the

You can use your Channel Divinity feature to invoke the wrath of thunderstorms. When you deal lightning or thunder damage, you can use Storm’s Fury to deal the maximum damage on each of those damage dice instead of rolling them.

features.summary: You gain domain spells at the cleric levels listed in the
